title.narrative: Gemensamt FN Program Ending Violence phase II
UN Joint Programme Ending Violence phase II

description.narrative: Detta är ett fortsatt samarbete med UN för ett gemensamt program/JP för att stoppa våld mot kvinnor. UN Women är det ledande organet och UNDP och UNFPA deltar. JP EVaW fokuserar på tre av de fyra pelarna i Istanbulkonventionen: 1) Förhindra alla former av våld mot kvinnor; 2) Säkerställa effektivt skydd och tillhandahållande av lämpliga tjänster för överlevande; 3) Stödja utvecklingen och genomförandet av en effektiv och integrerad politik för våld mot kvinnor. Programmet riktar sig till alla kvinnor och flickor som har utsatts för våld. Särskilt fokus läggs på kvinnor och flickor som utsätts för diskriminering på flera grunder och intersektionella former. Dessutom engagerar projektet män och pojkar som centrala förändringsagenter för att främja jämställdhet mellan könen. UN-organen har ett nära samarbete med nationella partner, bland annat ministeriet för hälsa och socialt skydd, justitieministeriet, ungdomsministeriet, utbildningsministeriet, inrikesministeriet, den statliga polisen, lokala myndigheter, nationella människorättsinstitutioner, medier, det civila samhället och gräsrotsorganisationer.

This is a continued cooperation with UN for a Joint Programme/JP on ending violence against women. UN Women is the lead agency and UNDP and UNFPA are participating ones. The JP EVaW focuses on three of the four pillars of the Istanbul Convention: 1) Prevent of all forms of VAW; 2) Ensure effective protection and provision of adequate services for survivors; 3) Support the development and implementation of effective and integrated policies on VAW. The programme targets all women and girls who have experienced violence. It places a particular focus on women and girls who are subjected to multiple and intersecting forms of discrimination. Furthermore, the project engages men and boys as pivotal agents of change in the advancement of gender equality. The UN Agencies collaborate closely with national partners, including the Ministry of Health and Social Protection, the Ministry of Justice, the Ministry of Youth, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of the Interior, the State Police, Local Government Units, National Human Rights Institutions, the media, civil society and grassroots organisations, amongst others.

Project outcomes: 1.Women and girls enjoy more effective preventive measures against violence in Albania. 2.All women survivors and those at risk are better protected from all forms of violence and have equitable access to services in Albania. 3.Responsible institutions and actors implement national policies and legislation on VAW in a more comprehensive, inclusive and coordinated way in Albania.

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
The United Nations Joint Programme End Violence Against Women II (UN JP EVAW II) continued to support progress towards strengthening the prevention, response and policy environment around violence against women (VAW) in the country. Main results are listed below:
- There have been positive developments in strengthening the institutional set-up to address and combat VAW, with increased human resources and a newly established directorate in the Ministry dedicated to preventing and addressing violence against women.
- During 2024, there has been a sustained increase in the reporting of cases of VAW through the national hotline with a total of 4,658 calls in 2024, compared to 3,871 calls in 2023.
- The Femicide Watch was established jointly with the Ombudsperson of Albania, the first one in the region following the global methodology developed by UNODC and UN Women for data collection, and the first report highlighting the persistency of femicide cases in the country was published in December 2024.
- Two municipalities (Elbasan and Lushnja) increased their budget for delivering VAW services following an analysis of the municipalities financial gap for effectively addressing VAW cases, with a total increase of12 ALL 2,500,000.00 in the municipalities budget, which will be considered as an example and best practice for replication in other municipalities and supports gender responsive budgeting at local level.
- At least 19 civil society organizations (CSOs) have strengthened their capacities to engage in EVAW related policy processes, with 15 out of 16 recommendations shared by the Monitoring Network Against Gender Based Violence fully included in the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) report for Albania.
- Some 780 men and boys were involved in activities to raise awareness on gender equality, including through the strengthening of the Be a Man clubs across the country, boot camps for young students, workshops and dedicated workshops and sessions on positive fatherhood, and the annual Men who Inspire conference.
- Almost 3 million people were reached through social media, with great engagement especially during the International Womens Day (IWD) and the 16 days of activism campaign, and almost 5,000 people were directly engaged in in-person activities.
- Nearly 1,250 members of the Coordinated Referral Mechanism (CRM)in 43 municipalities, out of which more than 350 are men, have increased capacities to address violence against women, including police officers, health professionals, municipal staff, education professionals, and domestic violence (DV) coordinators amongst others. TAs part of these efforts, 256 police officers from 27 police stations across Albania received specialized training on implementing DV legislation, in collaboration with the Sector for Domestic Violence and Child Protection at the General Directorate of State Police.
- The Parliament of Albania was engaged in 2024, leading an initiative on addressing digital violence, with a dedicated analysis and assessment supported by the UN JP that paves the way for legal amendments.
- At least 43 media professionals (including 2 men) increased their capacities and raised their awareness about the role of the media in addressing stereotypes, and at least 10 media reports focused on reporting on violence against women, developed by the journalists attending the media forums.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
